clusters.rule: Use `Literal[...]` for Pydantic model fields whose valid values are an enumerable set of strings; do not encode the constraint only in the field description.
clusters.trigger: A Pydantic `Field(description='One of: ...')` or plain `str` field whose accepted values are a fixed, enumerable set
clusters.rationale: A description string is not validated; a Literal makes the contract enforceable and visible to type checkers and generated schemas.

clusters.rule: Provider code must import Task SDK symbols through `airflow.providers.common.compat.sdk`, never directly from `airflow.sdk.*`.
clusters.trigger: A direct `from airflow.sdk.<module> import <Symbol>` inside any file under `providers/`
clusters.rationale: Providers support multiple Airflow core versions; the compat shim is what keeps them installable against cores where the SDK module does not exist or lives elsewhere.

clusters.rule: Import an optional provider feature dependency lazily inside the function that needs it, rather than at module level, when other code paths in the same module work without that dependency.
clusters.trigger: A module-level `try: import <optional_dep> / except ImportError: raise AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` in a module where only one of several independent operator or toolset paths needs the dependency
clusters.rationale: A module-level raise makes the whole module unimportable, breaking operators that never touch the optional dependency.

clusters.rule: In the common.ai LangChain bridge `_sync_call`/`_async_call`, catch `pydantic_core.ValidationError` alongside `ModelRetry` and route it through `_handle_retry`.
clusters.trigger: An `except ModelRetry` clause in `langchain_bridge.py` that does not also catch `ValidationError`
clusters.rationale: Reviewer-identified gap in one specific bridge implementation rather than a standing repo-wide expectation.

clusters.rule: A sqlglot-based denylist of data-modifying SQL statements must include `exp.Command`, sqlglot's fallback node for unrecognised syntax, so unparsed statements fail closed.
clusters.trigger: A tuple/set of `exp.*` node types used to reject mutating SQL that omits `exp.Command`
clusters.rationale: Anything sqlglot cannot classify becomes `exp.Command`; omitting it lets arbitrary unrecognised DDL/DML slip past validation.

clusters.rule: Put imports at module scope; a function- or method-body import is only acceptable to break a genuine circular import, and must carry a comment naming the cycle it avoids.
clusters.trigger: An `import` / `from ... import` statement inside a function, method, test helper or fixture body without an adjacent comment explaining the circular-import reason
clusters.rationale: Hidden imports obscure a module's real dependency graph and defer import errors to runtime; the repo only tolerates them where a cycle makes module scope impossible, and wants that reason recorded.

clusters.rule: Mocks that stand in for a real interface must be specced — `MagicMock(spec=...)`, `spec_set=`, or `create_autospec` — including nested attributes; `MagicMock(autospec=True)` is a no-op keyword and does not spec anything.
clusters.trigger: A bare `MagicMock()` (or `MagicMock(autospec=True)`) substituted for a known type such as the Task SDK execution API `Client`, `RunContext`, `ToolsetTool`, or a credentials object, then given attributes the real type may not have
clusters.rationale: An unspecced mock fabricates any attribute, so tests keep passing when production code reads a field that no longer exists on the real object.

clusters.rule: Log messages in `airflow.providers.common.compat.connection` must interpolate the actual hook class name instead of hardcoding `BaseHook`.
clusters.trigger: A `log.debug`/`log.info` call in `get_async_connection` containing the literal `BaseHook` after the hook became a parameter
clusters.rationale: A stale hardcoded class name in one helper's log line; a specific fix, not a standing rule.

clusters.rule: Tests for `get_async_connection` with a custom `hook=` argument must cover both the `aget_connection` path and the sync `get_connection` fallback path.
clusters.trigger: A test exercising `get_async_connection(hook=...)` that asserts only on the async branch
clusters.rationale: A missing-branch-coverage note on one specific helper's tests.

clusters.rule: Do not collapse `None` to an empty container with `param or []` in an operator `__init__` when the empty value has distinct meaning in the downstream API call; keep `None` and the empty list distinguishable.
clusters.trigger: `self.param = param or []` in an operator `__init__` where `param` is forwarded to an external API and an explicit empty list means something (e.g. clearing permissions)
clusters.rationale: `or []` erases the caller's ability to express 'send an empty list', which for some remote APIs is a destructive-but-intended request distinct from 'omit the field'.

clusters.rule: When a provider operator or hook gains a new documented parameter or changes its documented behaviour (auth types, supported options), update the class docstring and the matching provider RST guide under `providers/<name>/docs/` in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: A new `__init__` parameter or a changed `:param ...:` docstring list in a provider operator/hook with no corresponding edit to `providers/<name>/docs/operators/*.rst` or `providers/<name>/docs/connections/*.rst`
clusters.rationale: The published provider guides are the user-facing documentation; code-only changes leave them silently wrong at release time.

clusters.rule: In RST documentation, write version milestones as "Airflow version X.Y.Z", not a bare "version X.Y.Z".
clusters.trigger: An RST sentence containing `version <n>.<n>` without `Airflow` immediately before it
clusters.rationale: Provider docs sit alongside provider version numbers, so a bare version string is ambiguous about which artefact it refers to.

clusters.rule: Use `timezone.utcnow()` for timestamps in provider code rather than `datetime.now()`/`datetime.utcnow()`, and never initialise a mutable timestamp as a class-level attribute.
clusters.trigger: A class attribute assigned `datetime.now()` or `datetime.utcnow()` outside `__init__` in a provider module
clusters.rationale: Airflow standardises on timezone-aware UTC timestamps, and a class-level default is evaluated once at import and shared by every instance.

clusters.rule: When a provider reads an attribute introduced in a newer Airflow minor than its minimum supported core, access it with `getattr(obj, 'attr', default)` instead of direct attribute access.
clusters.trigger: Direct attribute access on a core object for an attribute added after the provider's minimum supported Airflow version
clusters.rationale: Providers are installed against a range of core versions; direct access raises `AttributeError` on the older ones.

clusters.rule: Name provider migration files after the next unreleased Airflow/provider version; rename the file before merge if a new minor has been cut since the branch was opened.
clusters.trigger: A migration path under `providers/*/migrations/versions/` whose embedded version string is at or below the latest released version
clusters.rationale: The version in the filename is what tells operators which release first requires the migration; a stale one misleads upgraders.

clusters.rule: A provider compatibility shim that works around an older Airflow core API must carry a `# TODO: Remove once minimum supported Airflow version is X.Y` comment naming the exact version.
clusters.trigger: A version-compat override or workaround block in a provider with no `TODO: Remove` comment naming the version that retires it
clusters.rationale: Without the version marker nobody can tell when a shim becomes dead code, and they accumulate indefinitely.

clusters.rule: Edge provider `worker_api/routes/ui.py` routes must declare the standard security dependencies: `Depends(requires_access_view(...))` for authentication, and `GetUserDep` alongside `SessionDep` on any state-mutating (POST/PATCH/DELETE) handler.
clusters.trigger: A new `@ui_router.*` route without `requires_access_view` in `dependencies=`, or a mutating route taking `SessionDep` but no `GetUserDep`
clusters.rationale: These routes are reachable from the Edge worker UI; without the access dependency they are unauthenticated, and without the user dependency the mutation is unattributable in audit logs.

clusters.rule: When a FastAPI route can raise a new HTTP status code, add that code to the route decorator's `responses=` mapping.
clusters.trigger: A `raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_4xx_...)` in a handler body whose decorator does not list that status in `responses=`
clusters.rationale: The generated OpenAPI schema drives the generated clients and the published API docs; an undeclared status makes both wrong.

clusters.rule: FastAPI `Query`/parameter descriptions in provider routes must describe what the implementation actually accepts (e.g. do not advertise comma-separated multi-field ordering when only a single field is supported).
clusters.trigger: A `Query(..., description=...)` string in a provider route that promises behaviour the handler does not implement
clusters.rationale: The description ships in the generated OpenAPI spec and the API reference, so a wrong one becomes a documented but unsupported contract.

clusters.rule: FastAPI route handlers in provider packages must carry an explicit return type annotation matching the decorator's `response_model`.
clusters.trigger: A handler declared with `response_model=Foo` but no `-> Foo` return annotation
clusters.rationale: The annotation is what makes the handler's contract checkable by mypy rather than only at request time.

clusters.rule: A SQLAlchemy `before_create` DDL event listener must not permanently mutate shared metadata such as `table.indexes`; express dialect differences with dialect-scoped DDL that adds or skips instead of discarding.
clusters.trigger: `table.indexes.discard(...)` / `.remove(...)` inside an `@event.listens_for(Table, 'before_create')` listener
clusters.rationale: The MetaData object is process-global, so a discard performed for one dialect silently removes the index for every later use of that table in the same process.

clusters.rule: Edge provider frontend code must issue HTTP calls through React Query (`useQuery`/`useMutation`) layered over Axios, not by calling Axios directly from components.
clusters.trigger: A direct `axios.get/post/...` call inside a `.tsx` component in the Edge plugin UI
clusters.rationale: React Query owns caching, refetching and request state for this UI; bypassing it produces components with hand-rolled loading and staleness handling.

clusters.rule: Regenerate a provider's OpenAPI client whenever its source spec YAML changes, so spec and `openapi-gen/` output stay in sync under the `ts-compile-lint-ui` hook.
clusters.trigger: A change to `openapi/*.yaml` in a provider UI package with no matching regeneration of the generated client, or the reverse
clusters.rationale: The generated client is committed to the tree; a spec change without regeneration means the UI compiles against a contract the backend no longer serves.

clusters.rule: Provider `package.json` files must not list `npm` itself or single-letter packages such as `i` among their dependencies.
clusters.trigger: `"npm"` or `"i"` appearing as a key in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` of a provider `package.json`
clusters.rationale: These entries are the fingerprint of a mistyped `npm i` command and pull an entire package manager into the shipped dependency tree.

clusters.rule: A provider's prek/pre-commit hooks and their supporting scripts must live inside that provider's own directory, not in the repository root.
clusters.trigger: A hook entry in a provider `hatch_build.py` (or provider hook config) pointing at scripts outside `providers/<name>/`
clusters.rationale: Providers are released as independent distributions; root-level scripts are not part of the provider package and break for anyone working on it standalone.

clusters.rule: Provider log handlers must track airflow-core field renames on structured log records (e.g. `.message` becoming `.event`) and version-gate the access when both cores are supported.
clusters.trigger: Access to `.message` on a structured log record inside a provider log handler
clusters.rationale: The record shape is core-owned; providers reading the old field emit empty or broken log lines against newer cores.

clusters.rule: A provider log handler that receives the task-log location from task startup metadata must not re-query `TaskInstance` from the metadata database to work out where to write.
clusters.trigger: A `TaskInstance.get_task_instance(...)` (or equivalent DB lookup) inside a provider log handler's write/emit path
clusters.rationale: Log handlers run in the worker/task process, which is not supposed to hold a metadata DB connection; the location is already supplied to it.

clusters.rule: Extract repeated `test_client.app.dependency_overrides[...]` setup into a shared fixture instead of duplicating it in each test method.
clusters.trigger: Several test methods in one class repeating the same `dependency_overrides` assignment block
clusters.rationale: Generic de-duplication advice about test setup, not a repo-specific expectation.

clusters.rule: When re-raising a missing optional provider dependency as an `ImportError`, suppress the chained original with `raise ImportError(...) from None`.
clusters.trigger: `except ImportError: raise ImportError(...)` for an optional dependency without `from None`
clusters.rationale: The chained traceback adds noise the user cannot act on; the actionable message is the install hint alone.

clusters.rule: Give `timetable_type` a sensible default in the `DagModel` constructor so tests do not have to assign it on every instance.
clusters.trigger: Tests assigning `dag_model.timetable_type = ""` in setUp or individual test bodies
clusters.rationale: A one-off suggestion about a single new column's default, prompted by one PR's test churn.

clusters.rule: In `GitDagBundle._initialize()`, assign and properly close `self.repo` before any early return on the cached-version path when `prune_dotgit_folder=False`.
clusters.trigger: A new early `return` in `_initialize()` after `_local_repo_has_version()` that leaves `self.repo` unset
clusters.rationale: A specific leaked/unset-attribute defect introduced by one refactor of that method.

clusters.rule: Treat `GitDagBundle.version` as a commit-ish (tag, branch or short SHA) and resolve it with `repo.commit(self.version).hexsha` before comparing it against `repo.head.commit.hexsha`.
clusters.trigger: A string equality comparison between `self.version` and `repo.head.commit.hexsha` in a git bundle method
clusters.rationale: Bundle versions are user-supplied refs, not full SHAs, so raw string comparison reports a mismatch for a repo that is already at the right commit.

clusters.rule: Do not import underscore-prefixed internals of a third-party package (e.g. `google.genai._api_client`, `structlog._output.WRITE_LOCKS`); where such an import is unavoidable, wrap it in `try/except ImportError` with a `None` fallback, guard every use of it, and add tests that catch upstream removal.
clusters.trigger: An import of a symbol whose module path contains a leading-underscore component from a third-party package under `providers/` or `task-sdk/src/`
clusters.rationale: Private internals carry no compatibility promise, so a routine dependency upgrade can break DAG parsing or task execution outright unless the import is optional and guarded.

clusters.rule: Declare every package a provider imports directly as a direct dependency in that provider's `pyproject.toml`; do not rely on it arriving transitively.
clusters.trigger: An import of a top-level package that is absent from `dependencies` or the relevant extra in the provider's `pyproject.toml`
clusters.rationale: Providers are installed standalone, and a transitive dependency can be dropped by its parent at any release, breaking the import with no version constraint to explain it.

clusters.rule: Keep the public surface of provider operators, hooks and extractors backward compatible: a changed return value, changed traversal, or new constructor keyword must be opt-in via a new parameter defaulting to the legacy behaviour, and existing public signatures (e.g. `BaseExtractor.__init__(self, operator)`) must keep working.
clusters.trigger: A diff that changes an existing operator's `execute()` return shape, alters what an existing hook method traverses or returns, or passes a new required keyword to a subclass constructor unconditionally
clusters.rationale: These classes are third-party extension points and DAG-facing API; silently changing their contract breaks user DAGs and out-of-tree subclasses at upgrade time with no deprecation path.

clusters.rule: Raise native Python exceptions (`ValueError`, `TypeError`, `RuntimeError`) for argument validation and unexpected internal states in provider code and triggers, rather than `AirflowException`.
clusters.trigger: A new `raise AirflowException(...)` for parameter validation inside a provider hook, or for an internal error condition inside a `BaseTrigger.run()` coroutine
clusters.rationale: The project is deliberately decoupling providers from core exception types, and a validation bug is not an Airflow-level failure condition.

clusters.rule: When a trigger yields a `TriggerEvent` with `status: error` from a broad `except Exception`, prefix the message with the operation being performed rather than emitting the bare exception string.
clusters.trigger: `yield TriggerEvent({"status": "error", "message": str(err)})` inside a bare `except Exception` block
clusters.rationale: The event message is all the user sees in the task log; without the operation context an upstream error is untraceable to the call that produced it.

clusters.rule: When validation of a GCP resource identifier raises, the exception message must state every constraint the check enforces, including length bounds implied by the regex, not just the format.
clusters.trigger: A regex-based ID validation raising with a message that omits the length range the regex enforces
clusters.rationale: A user given only half the rule cannot fix their input from the message alone.

clusters.rule: Add a bullet to a provider's `changelog.rst` only when that provider's own source files change; a PR touching only another provider's tests gets no entry.
clusters.trigger: A new bullet in `providers/<name>/docs/changelog.rst` for a diff limited to test files of a different provider
clusters.rationale: Changelog entries drive provider releases and tell users what changed in the shipped package; test-only churn elsewhere changes nothing they can observe.

clusters.rule: Place forward-looking compatibility notes in a provider changelog above the upcoming release section, never inside or below an already-published release block.
clusters.trigger: A `.. note::` or compatibility banner inserted into or after an existing versioned release block in `changelog.rst`
clusters.rationale: Published release blocks are historical records; a note about future support inside one misattributes it to a release that never carried it.

clusters.rule: Add new provider documentation as `.rst` files wired into the existing docs structure, not as standalone `.md` files.
clusters.trigger: A new `.md` file added under `providers/*/docs/`
clusters.rationale: The provider docs are built by Sphinx from the RST tree; a Markdown file is never rendered or linked from the published site.

clusters.rule: Raise a dependency version floor — on a cross-provider `apache-airflow-providers-*` requirement or on an optional extra — only for a genuinely breaking change; an additive parameter with a `None` default or a new optional feature does not justify one.
clusters.trigger: A new or raised `>=x.y.z` constraint in a provider `pyproject.toml` accompanying a purely additive change
clusters.rationale: Every unnecessary floor narrows the installable version matrix and forces upgrades on users who do not use the new feature.

clusters.rule: Reuse Airflow's established name for a concept instead of inventing a synonym: `run_after` for the DAG run scheduling timestamp, `wait_for_completion` for the wait-for-finish flag, and an `a`-prefixed method name (`aget_connection`) for the async variant of an existing method.
clusters.trigger: A new or renamed parameter/method using `logical_date` or `date` for scheduling time, `wait_for_termination` for a completion flag, or an `async_`-prefixed name where a sync counterpart exists
clusters.rationale: These names appear across operators, hooks and the SDK; a synonym forces users to learn two vocabularies for the same concept and breaks the reader's ability to guess an API.

clusters.rule: Pass camelCase REST API field names (e.g. `definitionBody`, `routineType`) — not Python SDK attribute names (`body`, `type_`) — in the `fields`/update-mask argument of Google client update methods.
clusters.trigger: A writable-properties constant built from Python attribute names and passed as `fields` to a Google client update call
clusters.rationale: The update mask is sent to the REST API, which knows only its own field names; Python attribute spellings are silently ignored, so the update does nothing.

clusters.rule: Name provider system test files after the existing files in the same system-test folder; do not append a `_system` suffix.
clusters.trigger: A new file under `providers/*/tests/system/` named `test_<service>_system.py`
clusters.rationale: The system test runner and the docs that embed these files rely on the established naming; an off-pattern name is not picked up.

clusters.rule: Document a hook's connection configuration behaviour in its docstring: which `extra` keys are supported and in what precedence order, and exactly when a keyless fallback such as Application Default Credentials applies versus when an explicit key is still required.
clusters.trigger: A hook connection-init or auth method that adds conditional key-file skipping or several `extra.get(...)` branches without a matching `:param ...:`/docstring description
clusters.rationale: Connection setup is the part of a provider users configure by hand; undocumented precedence and fallback rules are only discoverable by reading the hook source.

clusters.rule: Read boolean Airflow configuration values with `conf.getboolean()`, never `conf.get()`.
clusters.trigger: `conf.get("<section>", "<key>", fallback=...)` for a key used as a boolean elsewhere
clusters.rationale: `conf.get` returns a string, so the literal `"False"` is truthy and the option silently cannot be turned off.

clusters.rule: Use the same `fallback=` value for every read of the same configuration (section, key) pair within a module.
clusters.trigger: Two or more `conf.get*()` calls for one (section, key) pair with different `fallback=` values in the same file
clusters.rationale: Divergent fallbacks make behaviour depend on which code path runs first when the option is unset.

clusters.rule: Provider documentation links must use the canonical `https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow-providers-<name>/` form; do not omit the `-providers-` segment.
clusters.trigger: An RST hyperlink to `https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow-<name>/`
clusters.rationale: The published docs are hosted under the providers path, so the short form is a dead link the moment the package is released.

clusters.rule: Each release version heading must appear exactly once in a provider's `changelog.rst`.
clusters.trigger: A version heading plus RST underline that already exists earlier in the same changelog file
clusters.rationale: Duplicate headings break the rendered changelog and the release tooling that parses it.

clusters.rule: Namespace a new provider by vendor, not by service: `package-name` in `provider.yaml` must be `apache-airflow-providers-<vendor>`, and a hook's `conn_type` must be vendor-qualified (e.g. `ibm_mq`) rather than a generic protocol category (`mq`).
clusters.trigger: A `provider.yaml` declaring `apache-airflow-providers-<vendor>-<service>`, or a hook declaring a generic `conn_type` such as `mq`, `queue` or `stream`
clusters.rationale: Amazon and Google consolidate every service under one vendor package, and `conn_type` is a global registry where a generic name collides with the next vendor implementing the same protocol.

clusters.rule: Instantiate `MessageQueueTrigger` with `queue=` carrying the full URI; `scheme=` takes only a scheme and raises `ValueError` at DAG parse time when given a URI.
clusters.trigger: `MessageQueueTrigger(scheme="<scheme>://...")` in a DAG or example
clusters.rationale: The failure happens during parsing, so the whole DAG file fails to import rather than the task failing at runtime.

clusters.rule: Items of `triggering_asset_events` are `AssetEvent` ORM objects: read their payload via the `.extra` attribute, not by dict-key subscription.
clusters.trigger: Square-bracket key access such as `event["payload"]` on an item iterated from `triggering_asset_events`
clusters.rationale: Subscripting the ORM object raises `TypeError` at task runtime, and example DAGs that do it are copied by users.

clusters.rule: Target `@patch` at the symbol as the module under test imports it; patching a path the module never imports is a silent no-op.
clusters.trigger: `@patch("airflow.providers.<pkg>.hooks.<module>.<name>")` where `<name>` is not imported by that module
clusters.rationale: Standard mock-library advice about patch targets, not a repo-specific expectation.

clusters.rule: Async hook tests must exercise the real method body with only the underlying I/O primitives patched, rather than patching the method under test itself.
clusters.trigger: `patch.object(hook, 'consume', side_effect=[...])` (or equivalent) replacing the very method the test claims to cover
clusters.rationale: Generic testing advice about not mocking the unit under test.

clusters.rule: A provider's docs requirements table must list exactly the packages declared in that provider's `pyproject.toml` dependencies — no extras, no omissions.
clusters.trigger: A row in the Requirements table of `providers/*/docs/index.rst` naming a package absent from the provider's `pyproject.toml`
clusters.rationale: The table is the published statement of what installing the provider pulls in; drift makes it a false promise.

clusters.rule: Every provider hook that declares a custom `conn_type` must have a matching `hooks:` block and `connection-types:` entry in the provider's `provider.yaml`.
clusters.trigger: A hook class with `conn_type = "<custom>"` and no corresponding `connection-types:` entry in `provider.yaml`
clusters.rationale: `provider.yaml` is what makes the connection type discoverable in the UI and the generated docs; without it the hook exists but users cannot configure a connection for it.

clusters.rule: Providers must not re-implement operators that already exist in airflow-core or the standard provider (e.g. `EmptyOperator`); point users at the core operator instead.
clusters.trigger: A new provider operator whose behaviour duplicates a core/standard operator, such as a no-op or passthrough task
clusters.rationale: Duplicates fragment the operator surface users have to learn and drift from the core implementation's behaviour over time.

clusters.rule: Provider code (hooks, listeners, plugins) must not call `settings.configure_orm()`; ORM setup belongs to the scheduler/executor process that hosts the provider code.
clusters.trigger: A `settings.configure_orm()` call anywhere under `providers/`
clusters.rationale: Re-configuring the ORM from provider code re-points the session factory for the whole process, affecting every other component running in it.

clusters.rule: Provider unit tests must build `Connection` fixtures with the provider's own `conn_type`, not a generic type such as `http`.
clusters.trigger: A test under `providers/*/tests/` creating a `Connection(conn_type="http")` for a hook that declares its own `conn_type`
clusters.rationale: Hook lookup and connection-form behaviour key off `conn_type`, so a generic type tests a path users never take.

clusters.rule: Every `__init__.py` in an `airflow/providers/` namespace directory must contain the legacy pkgutil namespace line `__path__ = __import__("pkgutil").extend_path(__path__, __name__)`; empty or implicit-namespace `__init__.py` files are not acceptable.
clusters.trigger: A new `__init__.py` under `providers/` (or `airflow/providers/`) that is empty or omits the `extend_path` line
clusters.rationale: Providers are separately installed distributions sharing one `airflow.providers` package path; pkgutil namespaces are what let them coexist in the same environment.

clusters.rule: Use proper RestructuredText footnote syntax in provider docs rather than plain bracketed numbers like `[1]`.
clusters.trigger: A `[N]` reference in `providers/*/docs/*.rst` that is not a real RST footnote or citation
clusters.rationale: A bare bracketed number renders as literal text with no link to its target.

clusters.rule: When a provider hook is fully async, the operator on top of it must wait exclusively through defer/trigger; do not add a synchronous polling path gated by `deferrable=False`.
clusters.trigger: A non-deferrable `while True` / `time.sleep` polling loop added to an operator whose hook is async
clusters.rationale: A blocking loop occupies a worker slot for the whole wait, which is precisely what the async hook and trigger exist to avoid.

clusters.rule: Adding deferrable mode to a provider operator requires both an update to that operator's RST docs page and a `providers/<pkg>/newsfragments/<pr>.feature.rst` newsfragment.
clusters.trigger: A diff adding `self.defer(...)` to a provider operator with no newsfragment file and/or no operator docs update
clusters.rationale: Deferrable mode is a user-visible feature that must appear in the provider's release notes and in the guide users configure it from.

clusters.rule: Build Azure blob names and paths with `posixpath.join`, never `os.path.join`.
clusters.trigger: `os.path.join` used to construct a blob name or path in an Azure hook or transfer
clusters.rationale: Blob names are always forward-slash separated, so `os.path.join` produces backslash-separated names on Windows workers.

clusters.rule: Use `str.removeprefix()` rather than `str.replace(prefix, "", 1)` when stripping a known leading prefix.
clusters.trigger: `.replace(prefix, "", 1)` used to strip a leading path prefix
clusters.rationale: General Python idiom advice that carries no repository-specific judgement.

clusters.rule: A trigger's timeout branch must always yield a `TriggerEvent` carrying the timeout status and a descriptive reason: do not `break`/`return` out of the polling loop, and wrap any cancellation side-effect in its own try/except so a failed cancel cannot replace the timeout event.
clusters.trigger: A polling loop in `providers/*/triggers/*.py` that reaches its timeout condition and breaks without yielding, or performs a cancel call in the timeout branch outside a dedicated try/except
clusters.rationale: A trigger that ends without yielding leaves the deferred task hanging, and a cancellation error surfacing instead of the timeout reports the wrong cause to the user.

clusters.rule: An `AirflowPlugin` subclass docstring must describe only the events the plugin actually registers and handles.
clusters.trigger: A plugin docstring claiming to handle event types (e.g. DAG run events) that the plugin body does not implement
clusters.rationale: Plugin docstrings are how integrators decide what a listener covers; an aspirational one leads them to expect callbacks that never fire.

clusters.rule: Assertions on `trigger.serialize()` must check that the result is a tuple, that the class path string matches the trigger's `__module__`/`__name__`, and that the full kwargs dict is as expected.
clusters.trigger: A test destructuring `trigger.serialize()` without verifying the tuple type or the fully-qualified class path
clusters.rationale: The serialized class path is what the triggerer uses to rebuild the trigger, so a wrong or moved path only fails in production if the test does not assert on it.

clusters.rule: Build trigger deadline values in tests with the same clock the trigger implementation uses; never mix `time.time()` in the test with `time.monotonic()` in the trigger.
clusters.trigger: A test constructing a deadline such as `END_TIME = time.time() + ...` for a trigger whose implementation reads `time.monotonic()`
clusters.rationale: The two clocks have unrelated epochs, so the deadline is meaningless and the test asserts on accidental behaviour.

clusters.rule: A task log handler's `delete_local_copy` must remove only the uploaded log file (`path.unlink()`), never its parent directory via `shutil.rmtree()`.
clusters.trigger: `shutil.rmtree(os.path.dirname(log_file))` in a task log handler's upload-and-delete path
clusters.rationale: The parent directory holds logs for other attempts and tasks, which the handler has no business deleting.

clusters.rule: A `ClassVar` dict used as an in-process cache in a provider utility is acceptable because provider worker processes are short-lived.
clusters.trigger: A reviewer questioning whether a `ClassVar[dict]` cache in a provider utility can grow unboundedly
clusters.rationale: This records the answer to a review question rather than an expectation a diff can violate.

clusters.rule: Read fields that exist directly on the `DagRun` model (e.g. `dagrun.team_name`) from the object itself instead of re-deriving them through `dag_version_info()`.
clusters.trigger: A `cls.dag_version_info(dagrun, "field_name")` call for a field that is a plain attribute on `DagRun`
clusters.rationale: The indirection adds a lookup that can disagree with the authoritative attribute on the run.

clusters.rule: Redis provider triggers and queue providers must take host and port exclusively from `redis_conn_id`; do not parse `host:port` out of the queue URI.
clusters.trigger: A Redis queue provider or `AwaitMessageTrigger` that parses host/port from the queue URI string
clusters.rationale: Connection details belong in the Airflow connection so credentials and TLS settings stay in one managed place rather than inline in DAG code.

clusters.rule: When refactoring the OpenLineage extractor manager's no-extractor branch, keep the `unknownSourceAttribute` facet and the inlets/outlets fallback intact under the default `hook_lineage=True` configuration.
clusters.trigger: A change to the else/elif branching around `extract_metadata`'s no-extractor path in `openlineage/extractors/manager.py`
clusters.rationale: Describes a specific regression a single refactor introduced in one branch, not a standing rule.

clusters.rule: Update `tests/unit/openlineage/plugins/test_manager.py` whenever the OpenLineage extractor manager's branching changes.
clusters.trigger: A change to `openlineage/extractors/manager.py` with no corresponding test change
clusters.rationale: Generic keep-tests-in-step advice tied to one file pair.

clusters.rule: When a provider moves an import from an airflow-core module to `airflow.providers.common.compat.sdk`, bump the provider's minimum required airflow-core version indicator used by the release manager in the same change.
clusters.trigger: A diff replacing `from airflow.listeners import ...` (or another core import) with the `common.compat.sdk` equivalent without touching the minimum core version
clusters.rationale: The compat module only provides the symbol from a certain core version onwards, so the declared minimum is what stops the provider being installed where the import fails.

clusters.rule: Do not call `logging.shutdown()` from a provider listener without proving the call cannot affect global Airflow logging.
clusters.trigger: A `logging.shutdown()` added inside a provider's listener plugin
clusters.rationale: Listeners run inside the scheduler and task processes, so shutting logging down there silences the host component's own logs.

clusters.rule: The install hint in an `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` must read `pip install --upgrade <package>`, not a bare `pip install <package>`.
clusters.trigger: An `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` message containing an install hint without `--upgrade`
clusters.rationale: The dependency is usually already installed at too old a version, so a plain install is a no-op and the user is left stuck.

clusters.rule: In the Postgres hook, do not skip psycopg3 notice logging with an early return when `enable_log_db_messages=True`; implement the psycopg3 notice handling instead.
clusters.trigger: `if USE_PSYCOPG3 or not self.enable_log_db_messages: return` before the notice-logging loop in `postgres.py`
clusters.rationale: A specific shortcut taken in one psycopg3 migration PR, not a general expectation.

clusters.rule: A retryable-error tuple in the Postgres hook must list the narrowest psycopg exception subclasses (e.g. `UndefinedColumn`, `UndefinedTable`) from the matching package — `psycopg` for v3, `psycopg2` for v2 — never a broad class such as `OperationalError`.
clusters.trigger: A `_POSTGRES_RETRYABLE_ERRORS` tuple containing `OperationalError` or another broad psycopg exception class
clusters.rationale: Retrying on a broad class re-runs statements after genuine connection and authentication failures, turning a clear error into repeated timeouts.

clusters.rule: Assert a mock was called exactly once (`assert_called_once()` or a `call_count` check) before inspecting `call_args`.
clusters.trigger: Access to `mock_*.call_args` with no preceding call-count assertion
clusters.rationale: Standard mock-library advice with no repository-specific content.

clusters.rule: Type-stub packages (`types-*`) belong in a provider's dev/type-check dependency group, never in its runtime `[project] dependencies`.
clusters.trigger: A `types-*` package added to the runtime `dependencies` list of a provider `pyproject.toml`
clusters.rationale: Stubs are build-time artefacts; shipping them forces every runtime install to pull packages that do nothing at runtime.

clusters.rule: Initialise expensive provider clients and connections in a `@cached_property`, not eagerly in `Hook.__init__`.
clusters.trigger: A provider client, session or sub-hook constructed directly in `Hook.__init__`
clusters.rationale: Hooks are instantiated during DAG parsing and templating where no connection should be opened; the cached property defers the work to first real use.

clusters.rule: Provider logo and image assets must live under the `providers/` tree, not in a parallel top-level `registry/` folder.
clusters.trigger: Image or logo files added under `registry/` rather than `providers/<name>/`
clusters.rationale: Assets outside the provider directory are not part of the released provider distribution.

clusters.rule: Test whether a sentinel is unset with the `is_arg_set()` helper from `airflow.serialization.definitions.notset` rather than an inline `is NOTSET` comparison, and annotate the parameter with `ArgNotSet` in its type signature.
clusters.trigger: An `if value is NOTSET` check without `is_arg_set()` and without `ArgNotSet` in the parameter annotation
clusters.rationale: The helper and the annotation are what make the unset sentinel visible to type checking and serialization; inline identity checks silently diverge from it.

clusters.rule: Extract repeated `str | datetime | None` type-dispatch into a shared utility rather than duplicating the `isinstance` block per method.
clusters.trigger: The same `isinstance(value, (str, datetime.datetime))` dispatch block repeated in more than one method
clusters.rationale: Generic de-duplication advice with no repository-specific content.

clusters.rule: Pass the Alembic revision message as a single quoted string rather than `"${@}"` when generating migrations from a shell script.
clusters.trigger: `"${@}"` passed as the `-m` argument to `alembic revision --autogenerate`
clusters.rationale: A one-off quoting bug in a single container script.

clusters.rule: A behaviour change to a public provider hook method — different return shape, different filtering — must be recorded in that provider's `docs/changelog.rst` under the next release.
clusters.trigger: A diff altering the return value or filtering logic of an existing public hook method with no changelog entry
clusters.rationale: Users pin provider versions and read the changelog to decide whether an upgrade is safe; an unannounced behaviour change breaks their DAGs without warning.

clusters.rule: A process-wide singleton pool must not implement `__aenter__`/`__aexit__`; expose an explicit lifecycle hook instead of pretending to have a scoped lifetime.
clusters.trigger: `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` added to a class that registers itself in a module-level `_instances` dict
clusters.rationale: Context-manager syntax invites callers to close a resource shared by every other user of the singleton in the process.

clusters.rule: Put `AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS` version gating for notifier behaviour in `BaseNotifier` rather than repeating the guard in each concrete notifier.
clusters.trigger: An `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS:` guard added inside a concrete `Notifier.__init__` or `notify()`
clusters.rationale: Every notifier faces the same core-version difference, so a per-notifier guard guarantees some of them are eventually missed.

clusters.rule: Log the error response body before calling `response.raise_for_status()` against a provider API.
clusters.trigger: A `response.raise_for_status()` with no preceding log of the response body on 4xx/5xx
clusters.rationale: `raise_for_status` discards the body, which is where these vendor APIs put the actual reason for the rejection.

clusters.rule: Expose the timeout for a long-running provider API call as a constructor parameter on the operator/hook rather than fixing it in a module-level constant.
clusters.trigger: A module-level `*_TIMEOUT` constant gating an HTTP request to an ML/agent/query workload with no matching constructor parameter
clusters.rationale: How long these workloads take is deployment-specific; a module constant leaves users no way to adjust it short of patching the provider.

clusters.rule: In a deferrable operator, push the query/job identifier to XCom as soon as it is obtained, before entering the poll or defer, not after the wait completes.
clusters.trigger: An `xcom_push` for a query/job id placed after the polling loop in a deferrable operator's `execute`
clusters.rationale: If the task fails or is killed during the wait, the identifier is the only way to find and clean up the remote job — and it is lost if it was never pushed.

clusters.rule: Handle symbols that moved or were added across versions with `try/except ImportError` fallbacks — stdlib first, then the backport — rather than `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS` version branches.
clusters.trigger: An `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS: from airflow.sdk... else: from airflow.sensors...` import split, or a bare `from typing_extensions import NotRequired` with no stdlib guard
clusters.rationale: The import either works or it does not; testing for it directly stays correct across the whole supported version range without a table of version constants to maintain.

clusters.rule: Mutate an Airflow `ContextVar` with the token/reset pattern — capture the token from `.set()` and `.reset(token)` in a `finally` — following the precedent in `initdb()`.
clusters.trigger: A `ContextVar.set()` whose token is not stored and never `.reset()` in a `finally` block
clusters.rationale: Without the reset the variable leaks into whatever runs next on the same context, which in a scheduler or test process is unrelated work.

clusters.rule: Do not assert on log output with `caplog`; assert on observable behaviour or return values instead.
clusters.trigger: A test importing or using pytest's `caplog` fixture to assert on logged messages
clusters.rationale: Log text is not part of the contract under test, and structlog configuration in this repo makes capture-based assertions fragile.

clusters.rule: Tests for SecretsMasker exception redaction must traverse the whole exception chain: attach a secret via `__cause__`/`__context__` and assert it is redacted, and include a cross-attribute cycle (`exc1.__cause__ = exc2; exc2.__context__ = exc1`) to prove the visited-set guard holds.
clusters.trigger: A redaction test that only inspects `exc.args`, or a circular-chain test that covers only same-attribute cycles
clusters.rationale: Secrets leak through chained exceptions as readily as through the primary one, and the cycle guard is exactly the code a same-attribute-only test cannot exercise.

clusters.rule: Task SDK documentation examples showing an async `@task` function must include the enclosing `@dag`-decorated wrapper so the snippet is a runnable DAG file.
clusters.trigger: An `.rst`/`.md` example defining an `@task` function and calling it at module level with no `@dag` function around it
clusters.rationale: Users copy these snippets verbatim; a fragment that calls a task at module level does not parse as a DAG.

clusters.rule: The `check_provide_session_kwargs` hook tests must cover the bypass path where an allowlist entry is removed or newly added, not only where an existing entry's count is loosened.
clusters.trigger: Tests for `_expand_for_allowlist_edits` exercising only the increased-count case
clusters.rationale: A specific coverage gap identified in one PR's tests.

clusters.rule: Pre-commit hook tests must pass `Path.resolve()`d paths so they match the production hook's path normalisation.
clusters.trigger: A hook test passing a raw path where the production code calls `Path(f).resolve()` before comparing
clusters.rationale: A specific mismatch corrected in one PR's tests.

clusters.rule: A shared metrics registry must key every instrument type the same way, or keep separate sub-maps per instrument type, so gauges and histograms cannot collide in one slot.
clusters.trigger: A `MetricsMap`-style registry keying one instrument type by name alone and another by name plus tags, or storing all instrument types in one dict
clusters.rationale: Mixed key schemes in one dict let a gauge silently overwrite a histogram registered under the same name.

clusters.rule: When a class reads an Airflow config value to supply an argument default, add a regression test that changes that config key before constructing the object and asserts the default is picked up.
clusters.trigger: An `__init__` reading `conf.get*` for a default with no test that constructs the class after modifying that section/key
clusters.rationale: Config-driven defaults are easy to wire to the wrong section or key, and nothing else in the test suite exercises that lookup.

clusters.rule: Insert new entries into `airflow/sdk/__init__.py`'s `__all__` and lazy-import dict in alphabetical position, not appended at the end.
clusters.trigger: A symbol added to `__all__` or the lazy-import dict in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/__init__.py` out of alphabetical order
clusters.rationale: The alphabetical ordering is what keeps this heavily-edited public export list reviewable and merge-conflict-free.

clusters.rule: In the Java coordinator, register the stdout/stderr socketpair pipe readers before starting the connection accept loop.
clusters.trigger: `_accept_connections` called before `_register_pipe_readers` on the socketpair write-ends handed to the subprocess
clusters.rationale: A specific ordering defect in one coordinator implementation.

clusters.rule: Language-agnostic coordinator plumbing — `_start_server`, `_accept_connections`, socketpair setup — belongs in `BaseCoordinator`, not duplicated in each per-language coordinator.
clusters.trigger: A new coordinator under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/` re-implementing socket server startup or accept helpers that are not runtime-specific
clusters.rationale: Every language SDK needs the same socket handshake; duplicating it means each new language re-derives (and re-breaks) the same protocol details.

clusters.rule: A language coordinator's constructor arguments need only make sense for its own runtime; do not copy another coordinator's argument names or types for the sake of symmetry.
clusters.trigger: A coordinator given argument names or types mirroring a different language's coordinator rather than idiomatic ones for its runtime
clusters.rationale: These coordinators are configured independently per language, so forced signature symmetry buys nothing and produces arguments that read wrongly in context.

clusters.rule: In Task SDK coordinator modules, log caught exceptions with `exc_info=True` as a structlog keyword rather than `error=str(exc)`.
clusters.trigger: `log.debug(..., error=str(exc))` or `log.warning(..., error=str(exc))` under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/`
clusters.rationale: Stringifying the exception throws away the traceback, which is the only thing that makes these subprocess failures debuggable.

clusters.rule: Do not define a `__version__` attribute inside `airflow.sdk.coordinators.*` sub-packages; the distribution version is exposed only as `airflow.sdk.__version__`.
clusters.trigger: A `__version__ = "..."` assignment or `"__version__"` in `__all__` under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/*/`
clusters.rationale: Per-subpackage versions imply independent release cadences that do not exist and drift from the real distribution version.

clusters.rule: Wrap every datetime placed into a callback context dict with `coerce_datetime` from `airflow.sdk._shared.timezones`, matching `RuntimeTaskInstance.get_template_context()` and the triggerer-side context builder.
clusters.trigger: A context dict in `callback_supervisor.py` populated with datetime fields from `DagRunResult` or similar without `coerce_datetime()`
clusters.rationale: Template code and user callbacks expect `pendulum.DateTime` throughout the context; a raw datetime breaks the pendulum-only methods users call on it.

clusters.rule: When renaming a message class in `task-sdk/.../execution_time/comms.py`, update the hardcoded message-type allowlists in `airflow-core/tests/unit/dag_processing/test_processor.py` and `airflow-core/tests/unit/jobs/test_triggerer_job.py` in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: A renamed `ToTask`/`ToSupervisor` message class with no corresponding edit to the allowlists in those two core test files
clusters.rationale: Those allowlists are the sync check between SDK and core message types; leaving them stale breaks the core test suite for an SDK-only change.

clusters.rule: Accumulate partition keys for a task instance in a set rather than a list, matching how asset aliases deduplicate repeated keys.
clusters.trigger: A `attrs.field(factory=list)` partition-keys field on a task-instance context object appended to without deduplication
clusters.rationale: Repeated keys are expected during a run, and the downstream consumers treat them as a set anyway.

clusters.rule: In Asset lookup code, treat `Asset(uri=...)` as having `name == uri` — the DB storage convention — instead of adding `name is None` branches as a distinct state.
clusters.trigger: None-guarded name/uri paths added to Asset or AssetRef handling in `task-sdk/.../execution_time/context.py` without normalising an absent name to the uri
clusters.rationale: The database never stores a null asset name, so a `None`-name branch is unreachable state that diverges from what lookups actually match against.

clusters.rule: A concrete Task SDK class exported from the public API must implement every abstract method of its base (including `to_upstream()` on partition mappers); leave it abstract or unexported until it does.
clusters.trigger: A concrete mapper under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/partition_mappers/` inheriting `RollupMapper` without overriding `to_upstream()`
clusters.rationale: Anything exported from `airflow.sdk` is a supported API users will instantiate; a partially implemented class fails at DAG runtime instead of at import.

clusters.rule: When a Task SDK API method queries only the metadata database and deliberately skips secrets backends (e.g. `Variable.keys()` versus `Variable.get()`), document the asymmetry and its reason in a `.. note::` block in the docstring.
clusters.trigger: A new listing method in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/variable.py` with no note about secrets-backend exclusion
clusters.rationale: Users reasonably assume the whole Variable API consults the configured secrets backend; the silent exception produces confusing partial results.

clusters.rule: Exceptions defined in `airflow/sdk/exceptions.py` that are only raised inside the Task SDK must not be imported by airflow-core, including its tests; their tests live in the SDK test tree.
clusters.trigger: An import from `airflow.sdk.exceptions` in airflow-core source or `airflow-core/tests/`
clusters.rationale: The SDK is a separately versioned distribution; a core import of an SDK-private exception recreates the coupling the split exists to remove.

clusters.rule: `supervise_callback` must call `_make_process_nondumpable()` before spawning its subprocess, exactly as `supervise_task` does.
clusters.trigger: A `supervise_callback` in `callback_supervisor.py` that spawns a subprocess without `_make_process_nondumpable()`
clusters.rationale: Callback processes hold notifier tokens and connection passwords in memory; without the dumpable flag cleared a core dump writes them to disk.

clusters.rule: Pass `context` to a callback callable only when `accepts_context` is true and the context value is not `None`; never forward `context=None`.
clusters.trigger: `**callback_kwargs` forwarded unconditionally when `accepts_context()` is true, without checking the context is not None
clusters.rationale: User callbacks that declare a context parameter assume it is populated; handing them `None` fails inside third-party code rather than at the call site.

clusters.rule: Exception log calls in `callback_supervisor.py` must carry structured identifying fields (`callback_id=`, `pid=`), mirroring the `ActivitySubprocess` pattern in `supervisor.py`.
clusters.trigger: A `log.exception(...)`/`log.error(...)` in `callback_supervisor.py` without `callback_id` or `pid` keywords
clusters.rationale: Callbacks run concurrently, so an unlabelled traceback cannot be attributed to the callback that failed.

clusters.rule: Size-limit warnings and API error messages in task-SDK execution code must name the worker-side `[workers] state_store_backend` option as the remedy, using the same section name in the asset-store warning and the API errors.
clusters.trigger: A size-limit warning or HTTP error in task-sdk execution code naming a `[state_store] backend` option
clusters.rationale: A specific wrong-config-section fix in one PR's message text.

clusters.rule: When instantiating a user-configured class from a config classpath (`import_string(spec.classpath)(**spec.kwargs)`), catch `ImportError`/`TypeError` and re-raise naming the offending key and classpath, and assert the result `isinstance` of the expected base class before caching it.
clusters.trigger: An `import_string(<spec>.classpath)(**<spec>.kwargs)` for a config-driven plugin or coordinator with no error wrapping and no base-class check
clusters.rationale: The raw exception names none of the user's configuration, leaving a misconfigured deployment with a traceback that does not identify the offending entry.

clusters.rule: When client-level exception translation replaces an existing error path, keep end-to-end coverage at the supervisor level: replace the removed `test_supervisor.py` test with one asserting the new exception propagates from `ActivitySubprocess.start()`/`supervise` and the child process is killed.
clusters.trigger: A diff deleting a test from `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/execution_time/test_supervisor.py` while adding the equivalent coverage only in `tests/task_sdk/api/test_client.py`
clusters.rationale: The client-level test proves the translation happens; only the supervisor test proves the supervisor reacts to it and reaps the child.

clusters.rule: Tests that keep a task subprocess alive to exercise signal delivery must bound their worst case to tens of seconds; do not write operator bodies like `for i in range(1000): sleep(1)`.
clusters.trigger: A test operator whose `execute` sleeps in a loop with a worst-case total well beyond a minute
clusters.rationale: If the signal under test fails to arrive, the unbounded sleep becomes the CI job's timeout rather than a fast, legible test failure.

clusters.rule: Use `partition_key` only for exact-match asset-event filtering; any regex or pattern value must go through `partition_key_pattern`, in tests as well as production code.
clusters.trigger: `partition_key=` set to a value containing regex metacharacters in a `GetAssetEventByAsset` message or asset-event query
clusters.rationale: The exact-match field is compared literally, so a pattern passed there matches nothing while looking like it should work.

clusters.rule: A regression test for a new `sys.exit(...)` inside `run()` must assert more than `SystemExit(1)`: it must also verify `on_failure_callback`, the `on_task_instance_failed` listener and `email_on_failure` still fire for the failed task instance.
clusters.trigger: A task-runner test asserting only `pytest.raises(SystemExit)` or an exit code for a failure path introduced by a new `sys.exit()`
clusters.rationale: An early exit is exactly the change that can skip the failure-notification machinery, and an exit-code assertion cannot see that.

clusters.rule: New language-SDK task registration APIs should follow the two-step registration the Java and Go SDKs use — define the callable, then register the task against a Dag — so Dag-level arguments remain expressible; an inline `registerTask({dagId, taskId}, fn)` must be justified against that path.
clusters.trigger: A task registration entrypoint added or documented under `ts-sdk/` that binds dagId and taskId inline in one call
clusters.rationale: Whole-Dag definition in the language SDKs is planned; an API that binds the Dag identity into the task call has nowhere to put Dag-level arguments when it lands.

clusters.rule: Every `Socket` created by the ts-sdk coordinator must register an `error` handler at construction that writes the channel name and message to stderr.
clusters.trigger: A `Socket` constructed or stored under `ts-sdk/src/coordinator/` wiring only `data`/`close`/`connect` handlers
clusters.rationale: An unhandled socket `error` event terminates the Node task process outright, losing the task with no diagnostic.

clusters.rule: Client-side socket reconnection in a language SDK is only correct if the Airflow coordinator accepts a second connection on the same channel; when adding `scheduleReconnect`/backoff logic, verify and cover the coordinator-side re-accept path in the same PR.
clusters.trigger: Reconnect or backoff logic added to a ts-sdk coordinator socket, e.g. `sock.on("close", ...)` calling `this.scheduleReconnect()`
clusters.rationale: Reconnect logic against a coordinator that never re-accepts turns a single dropped connection into an infinite retry loop that looks healthy from the client side.

clusters.rule: A secrets backend cannot enforce a denial by raising alone: the backend-iteration loops (`_get_connection`, `_async_get_connection`, `_get_variable` in `execution_time/context.py` and the same pattern in `models/connection.py`) swallow every exception with `except Exception: continue`, so a new deny signal must be special-cased and re-raised there in the same change.
clusters.trigger: A secrets backend made to raise `PermissionError` or another auth-denied exception without changing the backend-fallthrough loops to re-raise it
clusters.rationale: Otherwise the deny is swallowed and lookup falls through to the next backend, turning an intended refusal into a silent bypass.

clusters.rule: In supervisor message handlers, do not guard Task SDK API client results with `isinstance(resp, XResponse)` plus an `else` branch; client methods return their response model unconditionally and raise `ServerResponseError` on failure, so call `XResult.from_api_response(resp)` directly like the neighbouring handlers.
clusters.trigger: An `isinstance(<resp>, <X>Response)` check with an `else` fallback around a `self.client.<resource>.<method>(...)` call in `supervisor.py`
clusters.rationale: The else branch is unreachable, and writing it suggests a failure mode the client contract does not have.

clusters.rule: Never print or log a `Connection`, a `ConnectionResult`, or `Connection.get_uri()` output in Task SDK execution paths, including temporary debug prints.
clusters.trigger: A `print(...)` or logging call interpolating a `Connection`, `conn_result` or `get_uri()` under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/`
clusters.rationale: The connection URI carries the password in cleartext and these logs are shipped to the task log store users and operators can read.

clusters.rule: A tracing helper that no-ops below a configured OTel detail level must return `contextlib.nullcontext(trace.INVALID_SPAN)`, not `trace.INVALID_SPAN` itself, so `with detail_span(...) as span` still works and yields `INVALID_SPAN`.
clusters.trigger: A span wrapper whose disabled branch returns `trace.INVALID_SPAN` while `__enter__` calls `self._ctx.__enter__()`
clusters.rationale: Returning the span directly removes `__enter__`/`__exit__`, so every call site raises as soon as the detail level is lowered — the configuration that was supposed to be the safe one.

clusters.rule: Do not wrap conn-id filesystem injection for `ObjectStoragePath` in a blanket `except Exception: pass`; set the cached filesystem through `self.fs` and either let the error propagate or suppress only the specific provider-unavailable/scheme-unregistered errors while logging at debug.
clusters.trigger: `attach(...).fs` assigned to `__wrapped__._fs_cached` (or similar) under a bare `except Exception: pass` in `sdk/io/path.py`
clusters.rationale: The blanket suppression turns a misconfigured connection into a path that silently uses the wrong filesystem instead of failing where the user can see it.

clusters.rule: A comment or docstring that tells the reader to run a benchmark or helper script must name an entrypoint that exists in the tree (e.g. under `dev/`); otherwise add the script in the same PR or drop the instruction.
clusters.trigger: A comment or docstring pointing at a `dev/...` script or other repo entrypoint that is not present in the repository
clusters.rationale: An instruction naming a file nobody can find wastes the next reader's time and cannot be distinguished from a rename that was missed.
